steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Age, class, and disability are under-analysed but important aspects of media representation, affecting how large sections of the population are perceived and treated.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Youth representation: young people are often stereotyped as lazy, rebellious, tech-obsessed, vulnerable, or dangerous. News media frequently portrays youth negatively — crime, anti-social behaviour, unemployment.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Elderly representation: older people are often invisible in media or stereotyped as frail, dependent, wise, or comical. Their underrepresentation reflects ageism in the media industries.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Middle-aged representation: often the 'default' in media — professionals, parents, authority figures. This age group is the most represented because it matches the demographic of media producers.
